# Whale sightings {#sec-app-whales}

[Informative]{.status}

Whale sightings were the framework's **proof of concept**.
They are a clear example of real-time situational awareness that current standards do not provide:
a sighting is useful to vessels nearby for minutes to hours, it may come from a mariner, a shore network or an automated detector,
and it needs to reach vessels whether or not they are connected to the internet.

## Flow

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "A sighting from origin to helm (illustrative)."
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Observer
  participant S as Shore sighting<br/>service
  participant SH as Shadow of<br/>Vessel B
  participant G as Vessel B<br/>gateway
  participant D as Vessel B<br/>display
  participant A as Vessel A AIS<br/>(AIS only)
  participant DA as Vessel A<br/>display
  O->>S: Report sighting<br/>(IP, signed)
  S->>SH: Notify of sighting in<br/>area of interest (IP)
  SH->>G: Deliver when<br/>connected (IP)
  G->>D: Present on<br/>chartplotter<br/>(NMEA 2000)
  S->>A: Broadcast via shore station<br/>(AIS)
  A->>DA: AIS message<br/>in a PGN<br/>(NMEA 2000)
```

At every step it is **the same sighting**: same identity, same meaning, same provenance —
carried at full fidelity over IP and in reduced form over AIS and NMEA 2000.
